insight.title: Jellyfish Sleep Without a Brain
insight.subtitle: A creature with absolutely zero thoughts still has to take a nap.

sections.text: Jellyfish have no brain, no heart, and are 95% water. Yet, scientists discovered that they still get tired and need to sleep every single night to function.
At night, they pulse 30% slower and ignore food. If scientists artificially wake them up, they spend the next day visibly groggy and sluggish.
It turns out sleep isn't a complex, high-level brain reboot. It is a fundamental tax of life that even a mindless bag of water is forced to pay.
Sleep is so simple, you don’t even need a brain.
